figures.finding: The Gambia's Labour Act 2023 defines a child as anyone under eighteen and forbids engaging a child in any public or private agricultural, industrial or non-industrial undertaking, subject to the Children's Act (vocational or training work aside); the Children's Act sets sixteen as the minimum age for light work (work not harmful to health or development and not affecting school), so a child may do light work from sixteen and full employment comes at eighteen (reading).

value.basis: Labour Act 2023 ss. 2, 54; Children's Act 2005 s. 43 (reading of the two together)

figures.applies: Labour Act 2023 (FAOLEX copy) and Children's Act 2005 (Rodra copy).

sources.said: “child” means a person below the age of eighteen years; ... (1) Subject to subsection (2) and the Children’s Act, a person shall not engage a child in any public or private agricultural, industrial or nonindustrial undertaking.

43. (1) The minimum age for the engagement of a child in light work is sixteen years. (2) Light work means work, which is not likely to be harmful to the health or development of the child and does not affect the child’s attendance at school or the capacity of the child to benefit from school work.

figures.finding: The Gambia has no child-performer permit: no child (under eighteen) may be engaged in any undertaking save light work from sixteen, never at night (20:00 to 06:00), never in exploitative or hazardous work; the law names no exception for performing, so a child actor, writer or director under sixteen can't be engaged (reading).
figures.applies: Children's Act 2005 ss. 41-43; Labour Act 2023 s. 54.

sources.said: 41. (1) A person shall not engage a child in exploitative labour. ... (2) Night work means work between the hours of eight o’clock in the evening and six o’clock in the morning.

figures.finding: No child (under eighteen) in The Gambia is capable of entering into any contract save as the Children's Act allows; a child's contracts other than for necessaries, for money lent or goods supplied, are voidable, and no action lies after majority on promises made before it. No set-aside of earnings was found; the rule reaches every contract (reading).

sources.said: 14. (1) Except as provided in this section, no child is capable of entering into any contract. (2) All contracts, except contracts for necessa- ries, entered into by a child for repayment of money lent or for payment of goods supplied to the child, shall be voidable.
